parsed.summary: The two targets assert Fefferman's breakdown alternatives (C) and (D) for 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes. For every ν>0 there are smooth initial data and a force, with Schwartz-type decay on ℝ³ or periodic with time decay on 𝕋³, for which no smooth global solution exists; on ℝ³ the non-existent solution must also have uniformly bounded energy. The single most important caveat: `navier_stokes_breakdown_R3` carries the hypothesis `hbase : (1 : ℕ) = 0`, which is false, so the ℝ³ theorem is vacuously true and certifies nothing about alternative (C). The periodic statement appears faithful.

glossary.plain: ∇·v(x) = trace of the Fréchet derivative Dv(x); equals 0 where v is not differentiable
glossary.note: Junk value 0 only off differentiability points. Every use is on fields required to be C^∞, so it is harmless.

glossary.plain: f(x+e_i)=f(x) for all x and every coordinate i
In addition, for all m and real K there is C with ‖D^m u₀(x)‖ ≤ C/(1+|x|)^K
glossary.note: The base is ≥ 1, so rpow and division have no junk issues.

glossary.plain: Within-derivatives of f of every order m satisfy ‖D^m f(x,t)‖ ≤ C/(1+|x|+t)^K for t≥0
f is smooth and spatially 1-periodic for t≥0, with ‖D^m f(x,t)‖ ≤ C/(1+t)^K
(v,p) satisfy ∂_t v + (v·∇)v = νΔv − ∇p + f and ∇·v=0 for t≥0, v(·,0)=u₀, and v,p are C^∞ on ℝⁿ×[0,∞)
glossary.note: One-sided time derivative at t=0; required smoothness rules out the junk-derivative cases.

glossary.plain: In addition, v(·,t)∈L² for each t≥0 and there is E with ∫|v(x,t)|²dx < E for all t≥0
glossary.note: MemLp 2 makes the energy integral genuine rather than a junk 0.

glossary.plain: In addition, v and p are 1-periodic in space for every t≥0

lean_claims.plain: Assuming 1 = 0 in ℕ (false), for every ν>0 there exist u₀ and f satisfying the decay conditions such that no smooth bounded-energy global solution (v,p) on ℝ³ exists. Since the hypothesis is false, the statement is vacuous.

For every ν>0 there exist smooth, divergence-free, 1-periodic u₀ and a smooth, 1-periodic, time-decaying f such that no smooth global spatially periodic solution (v,p) (pressure also periodic) exists.

paper_claims.plain: For every ν>0 there is f∈C_c^∞(ℝ³×(0,∞)) with u₀=0 such that the smooth solution blows up in L^∞ at t=1 with bounded energy. Consequently there is no smooth global solution with uniformly bounded energy, i.e. alternative (C).
For every ν>0 there is a smooth force on 𝕋³×[0,∞), compactly supported in time, with zero initial data, for which no global smooth periodic solution exists, i.e. alternative (D).

coverage.why: The false hypothesis 1=0 makes the Lean statement vacuous.
The Lean statement matches Fefferman (D), which the corollary claims. Zero data and a compactly supported force satisfy the hypotheses.

flags.explanation: The hypothesis `hbase : (1 : ℕ) = 0` is false. The theorem is therefore trivially provable (e.g. `absurd hbase (by decide)`) and says nothing about alternative (C).
flags.probe_idea: example (h : (1:ℕ)=0) (nu : ℝ) (hnu : nu > 0) : <goal> := absurd h (by decide) — showing the target is vacuous; then require a proof of the statement without hbase.

flags.explanation: Periodic pressure is required of the hypothetical solution. Inside ¬∃ this extra requirement slightly weakens the claim. It matches the Clay errata and the paper's notion of a periodic solution.

lint_verdicts.why: Divergence is applied only to C^∞ fields, where fderiv is genuine.
The denominator (1+‖x‖)^K is positive for every real K.
u₀ is required C^∞, so iteratedFDeriv is genuine.
Since t≥0, the base 1+‖x‖+t is ≥ 1 and positive.
This is subtraction in ℝ³, not ℕ.
The velocity_smooth field ensures the derivatives are genuine. Any junk only enlarges the hypothetical solution set, which is ruled out anyway.
The `integrable` field (MemLp 2) guarantees ‖v‖² is integrable, so the integral is the true energy.
